content.value_statement: Complex agent tasks can exceed one context window and lose coordination quality. This skill helps you choose patterns, handoffs, consensus methods, and failure controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical agent patterns with practical tradeoffs.
Maps context isolation choices to task complexity and coordination needs.
Describes handoff protocols, direct forwarding, weighted voting, and debate methods.
Lists common failure modes, including bottlenecks, divergence, and error propagation.
Includes framework-oriented examples for LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI-style designs.
Provides small Python utilities for in-memory agent messages, voting, and failure handling.
limitations: It is architecture guidance, not a complete production agent framework.
Code snippets are illustrative and need integration, validation, and security review.
It does not run, deploy, or monitor agents automatically.
External framework links may change after publication.

use_cases.title: Plan a Research Agent Team
use_cases.description: Select roles, handoffs, and aggregation steps for a research workflow with separate context windows.

use_cases.title: Choose an Architecture Pattern
use_cases.description: Compare supervisor, swarm, and hierarchy options before building an agent product feature.

use_cases.title: Review Coordination Risks
use_cases.description: Identify bottlenecks, divergence risks, weak consensus, and missing recovery controls in an existing design.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new agent workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a multi-agent workflow for this task: [task]. Recommend one architecture pattern and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Map Agents and Handoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for role boundaries and routing.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design agents, responsibilities, handoff rules, and shared state for this workflow: [workflow]. Keep context isolation explicit.

prompt_templates.title: Add Consensus Controls
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of decisions made by several agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: For this multi-agent design, propose weighted voting, debate, or validation controls: [design]. Include failure triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Production Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this multi-agent architecture for bottlenecks, divergence, error propagation, context leakage, and recovery gaps: [architecture].

output_examples.input: A team wants an agent system that researches competitors, analyzes findings, and writes a report.
output_examples.output: Use a supervisor pattern with researcher, analyst, and writer agents. Add direct forwarding for source-heavy sections and validate outputs before synthesis.

output_examples.input: A peer-to-peer agent design keeps looping between analysis and writing agents.
output_examples.output: Add clear handoff criteria, a time-to-live limit, convergence checks, and a fallback supervisor for unresolved loops.

output_examples.input: Several agents vote on a technical decision, but weak answers sway the result.
output_examples.output: Use weighted voting based on expertise and confidence. Add a debate round where agents must critique unsupported assumptions.

best_practices: Use multiple agents only when context isolation or parallel work provides clear value.
Define handoff contracts, shared state rules, stop conditions, and validation before implementation.
Test bottlenecks, divergence, failed workers, and weak consensus before production use.
anti_patterns: Creating agents to mirror job titles without a context or tool boundary.
Allowing unlimited handoffs or debates without convergence checks.
Forcing a supervisor to paraphrase specialist outputs when exact detail matters.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when one agent cannot manage the task context, tools, or parallel subtasks effectively.

faq.question: Does it create a working agent system?
faq.answer: No. It provides design guidance, examples, and small utilities that need implementation work.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it discuss?
faq.answer: It references LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI-style approaches for common multi-agent patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to agent workflows designed around Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How does it reduce context problems?
faq.answer: It separates subtasks into focused agent contexts and defines how results return to coordination layers.

faq.question: What should I review before production use?
faq.answer: Review tool permissions, data access, logging, failure handling, cost limits, and output validation.
